newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices rise further in week.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices rise further in week.

text.p: Limited supply saw auction prices continue their upward movement at sales in Sydney and Fremantle this week, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said.
The Wool International eastern market indicator ended the week at 714 cents a kg clean, up 14 cents on the week, while the western market indicator finished at 666 cents a kg clean, up eight cents.
This left the eastern indicator on a 21-month high.
A total of 39,332 bales were offered at auction, with a pass-in rate of eight percent.
The council said exporters confirmed that the market was presently supply-driven, with no reported changes in consumer demand fundamentals in some key northern hemisphere markets.
Restocking of the pipeline continued, although there were increasing concerns that Continental Europe was having difficulty operating at current price levels, it said.
Some traders and mills appeared to recognise that auction supplies would continue to be limited until spring shorn wool entered the market at end-September 1997.
Reports of a strengthening El Nino weather effect would also be causing concern over 1998/99 volume and quality, it said.
In the futures market a total of 253 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended Thursday.
Open interest increased by 107 contracts to close at 1,161. The near August contract closed 14 cents up at 869 cents a kg clean.
Wool International said it sold 30,206 bales in the week ended Thursday, reducing its stockpile to 1,623,418 bales.
Sales continue next week in Sydney and Melbourne with 54,600 bales rostered.
